disposition.reason: Neighbors appeal the Jericho DRB's approval of a PUD subdivision for three new duplexes (six dwelling units), which is new housing.

evidence.quote: appeal the Jericho Development Review Board’s (DRB) October 27, 2014 final plat subdivision approval authorizing a six-unit, three-duplex planned unit development (PUD)
upon which three duplexes (six units) will be constructed and is thus subject to PUD review

project.description: Six-unit, age-restricted (55+) planned unit development of three new duplexes on a 28.5-acre portion of a 143-acre parcel at 44 Raceway Road, Jericho; final plat subdivision approval.

evidence.quote: final plat subdivision approval authorizing Atwood Enterprises, Ltd. to develop a six-unit, three-duplex planned unit development (PUD) subdivision
upon which three duplexes (six units) will be constructed and is thus subject to PUD review
The Project is a two-lot subdivision; one lot contains three “footprint” lots, each with a duplex structure

discretion.description: Neighbors challenged the approval on notice posting, compliance with the PUD provisions (elderly-housing density bonus, pedestrian connectivity with neighboring developments 'wherever possible') and conformance with the Town Plan.

evidence.quote: Section 10.13.9.7 requires that a PUD provide for vehicular and pedestrian connectivity with neighboring developments wherever possible.
Appellants argue the Project fails to provide for pedestrian connectivity because it lacks sidewalks
Specifically, Appellants challenge the adequacy of the chosen location in two ways.

observed_status.description: The court approved the PUD subdivision subject to the DRB's 19 conditions and remanded only for the ministerial issuance of a zoning permit; no further review is shown.

evidence.quote: We therefore impose these conditions. We REMAND this matter to the Town Zoning Administer for the ministerial act of issuing a zoning permit
A Judgment Order accompanies this Decision. This completes the current proceedings before this Court.

evidence.quote: Brian and Catherine Stevens appealed WW-4-4309 to this Court. In a February 18, 2015 Order, this Court dismissed their appeal as untimely.
Based upon the evidence presented at trial, which was put into context by the site visit, the Court renders the following Findings of Fact.
Applicant proposes to be subject to all 19 conditions of the Jericho DRB’s October 27, 2014 Approval set out above as Finding of Fact number 48. We therefore impose these conditions.

judgments.note: Appeal of a DRB final plat approval for three new duplexes (six units): municipal appeal about new housing.
No literal 'de novo', but the court held a trial and site visit, made its own findings, decided compliance itself and imposed conditions: a de novo hearing.
Filing date stated (Dec 3, 2014); merits decision of Feb 4, 2016 'completes the current proceedings'; no further appeal shown.
Described as a two-lot subdivision (one lot with three duplex 'footprint' lots, one common-land lot); the count of new residential building lots is not clearly stated, so unknown.

Names are from the merits decision caption; the motion-entry notification list differs slightly (John Wilson, Marilyn Marshall). Neighbor status inferred from concerns about the adjacent Foothills development and its water supply, not stated outright.

The pedestrian-connectivity argument under a 'wherever possible' PUD standard and the notice-adequacy challenge are actual contentions that involve judgment; Appellants otherwise cited no specific conflicting provisions.
The decision does not show which contention was principal; notice posting and the density bonus also figured prominently.
The merits decision completes the Environmental Division proceedings; remand is only for the ministerial permit issuance; no Supreme Court appeal observed, but one cannot be ruled out.
The Stevens' appeal of the wastewater permit is a distinct proceeding in this court with no docket number given.
